name: stenny
description: Your lecture transcripts, summaries and glossaries from Stenny, for studying with Claude.
long_description:
Stenny records your lectures on your Mac or Windows PC and transcribes them locally. With this extension Claude can read them: ask what the lecturer said about a topic, go through a lecture, or get quizzed, and Claude answers from your transcripts with timestamps like "Lecture 3 [0:12:30]".

Everything stays on your computer: Claude gets clean text (no file paths, no microphone names), and the only change it can make is adding correct spellings of names and terms to a course glossary, so future transcripts get them right.

Needs Stenny installed on this computer (https://stenny.eu). Works in the Claude desktop app only, not on the web or on your phone.

tools.name: list_courses
tools.description: Your courses, how many lectures each has, and recorded talks

tools.name: list_lectures
tools.description: A course's lectures with date, length, topics and section headings

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: One lecture's transcript, in parts; can jump to a timestamp

tools.name: get_summary
tools.description: The AI-written summary of a lecture

tools.name: search_lectures
tools.description: Where something was said: lecture, date, timestamp and a snippet

tools.name: get_glossary
tools.description: A course's glossary: correct spellings of names and terms

tools.name: suggest_glossary_corrections
tools.description: Fix a misheard name or term in all future transcripts of a course

tools.name: suggest_glossary_terms
tools.description: Add correctly spelled names and terms to a course glossary

prompts.name: study
prompts.description: Start a study session on one course with its lectures
prompts.text: I want to study ${arguments.course} with my lecture transcripts from Stenny. Use the Stenny tools: list the lectures of ${arguments.course} first, read the summaries, and read the transcripts for details. Then help me learn it: give me a short overview of what the lectures covered so far and ask what I want to do (explain a topic, go through a lecture, quiz me, prepare for the exam). Cite passages as "Lecture N [h:mm:ss]". The transcripts are automatic, so check unclear terms against the glossary.
